key_insight: POD-filtered LES training data enable a neural surrogate to predict mean turbine-wake flows with three orders of magnitude lower mean squared error than training on unfiltered data.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate could accelerate marine hydrokinetic turbine layout optimization in natural waterways with complex bathymetry and interacting wakes.
method: Generate instantaneous flow fields using large eddy simulation at a real tidal river site.
Apply proper orthogonal decomposition and select modes to suppress background fluctuations while retaining wake information.
Train a 3D convolutional encoder–decoder to predict time-averaged velocity fields.
evidence_signal: At a real tidal river site under ebb tide conditions, POD filtering reduced mean squared error by three orders of magnitude at equivalent network size and training cost.
watch_item: Generalization to other sites, tidal conditions, and turbine layouts is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: A novel machine learning framework based on proper orthogonal decomposition for turbine wake flow predictions in natural waterways
